note: Reset entry, not-reset and the first control-class rows. Every expect value is read from the cited page image and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation.

vectors.cite: Initialization sequence figure, pdf 27; first instruction after reset runs, pdf 22
vectors.derivation: The initialization figure (pdf 27) starts counting at the MSYNC release: microcycle 0 is NACT, microcycle 1 is IAB (input starting program counter), microcycles 2 to 4 are NACT and the first BAR (output starting program counter) is in microcycle 5. So the reset entry unit is 5 cycles with one IAB access at offset 1. POL-RST-01: reset zero-fills R0-R7 and the status flags and clears INTFF; the IAB reply loads all 16 bits of R7, here the provider answers $0000 so R7 = $0000; R0-R6 stay 0 from the zero-fill (init values 1111..7777 are overwritten, status S and C and INTFF go from 1 to 0). The first instruction after the entry always runs (pdf 22), so prev_interruptible = 0. Run state goes RESET_PENDING -> RUNNING.

vectors.cite: Initialization sequence figure, pdf 27 (no IAB before MSYNC release)
vectors.derivation: POL-RST-01: a state that was never reset (all bytes zero, run state UNRESET) has not seen the MSYNC release that starts the initialization sequence (pdf 27), so the CPU has no program counter to fetch from. Stepping it reports a NOT_RESET unit of 0 cycles, makes no bus access and changes no state field.

vectors.cite: Control instructions table, CLRC row, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: The control table (pdf 56) prints CLRC as 0000 000 110 = $0006, 4 cycles, 'CLeaR Carry to zero', marked Not Interruptable, with only C in the status change column. The instruction fetch figure (pdf 28) puts the BAR at cycle 0 and the DTB at cycle 2 of a 4-cycle fetch, so the whole instruction is the fetch: FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000, 4 cycles. One word is fetched, so R7 = $1000 + 1 = $1001. Not interruptible, so prev_interruptible = 0. R0-R6 are untouched. Init C = 1, S = Z = OV = 0: C becomes 0, S, Z and OV stay 0.

vectors.cite: Control instructions table, EIS row, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: The control table (pdf 56) prints EIS as 0000 000 010 = $0002, 4 cycles, 'Enable Interrupt System. Not Interruptable.', with a blank status change column. The instruction fetch figure (pdf 28) puts the BAR at cycle 0 and the DTB at cycle 2 of a 4-cycle fetch, so the whole instruction is the fetch: FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000, 4 cycles. One word is fetched, so R7 = $1000 + 1 = $1001. Not interruptible, so prev_interruptible = 0 (init default 1). R0-R6 are untouched. Enabling the interrupt system sets INTFF (POL-INT-03). Init INTFF = 0 becomes 1. Init S = Z = OV = C = 1 all stay 1 (blank status change column).
